name: Locus of control
items_note: Items copied from https://ipip.ori.org/newSingleConstructsKey.htm, 10 November 2026, +keyed items first as the key page lists them. This is the Total scale; the key page also gives Internality, Powerful Others and Chance subscales that share items, which are not used.

source.paper: IPIP scale measuring a construct similar to the Internality, Powerful Others, and Chance scales (Levenson, H. (1981). Differentiating among internality, powerful others, and chance. In H. M. Lefcourt (Ed.), Research with the locus of control construct, Vol. 1 (pp. 15-63). Academic Press), International Personality Item Pool

licence.text: Public domain (IPIP). Permission is granted automatically for any person to use IPIP items for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial.

instructions: Describe yourself as you generally are now, not as you wish to be in the future. Describe yourself as you honestly see yourself, in relation to other people you know of the same sex as you are, and roughly your same age.

scales.name: Locus of control
scales.publishedName: Locus of Control: Total (I - [P + C]), IPIP scale similar to Levenson (1981)

items.text: Feel comfortable with myself.
Believe that my success depends on ability rather than luck.
Just know that I will be a success.
Come up with good solutions.
Love life.
Act comfortably with others.
Feel up to any task.
Like to take responsibility for making decisions.
Take the initiative.
Make a decision and move on.
Believe that unfortunate events occur because of bad luck.
Believe that the world is controlled by a few powerful people.
Feel that my life lacks direction.
See difficulties everywhere.
Habitually blow my chances.
Believe some people are born lucky.
Dislike taking responsibility for making decisions.
Am less capable than most people.
Dislike myself.
Feel that I'm unable to deal with things.

reliabilitySource: Coefficient alpha as given on the single-construct scoring key page, https://ipip.ori.org/newSingleConstructsKey.htm, and in the comparison table, https://ipip.ori.org/newSingleConstructs.htm, which says the IPIP and original scales were both given to the Eugene-Springfield Community Sample (IPIP alpha .86, original .80, correlation between them .63); accessed 10 November 2026.
